record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.context_brief: Periodic-point closing problem on the torus
record.original_question: Let G be the set of C^∞ diffeomorphisms of T^n isotopic to the identity that have no periodic points, and let Ḡ be its closure in the C^∞ topology. For n ≥ 2, does Ḡ have empty interior in Diff^∞_0(T^n)?

evidence.quote: Question. Does the closed set G have no interior (n ≥ 2) in Diff∞0(Tn) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\infty}_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ denote the group of $C^{\infty}$ diffeomorphisms of the $n$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ that are isotopic to the identity, equipped with the $C^{\infty}$ topology. Let
$$G = \{\, f \in \mathrm{Diff}^{\infty}_0(\mathbb{T}^n) : f \text{ has no periodic points} \,\},$$
and let $\overline{G}$ denote the closure of $G$ in $\mathrm{Diff}^{\infty}_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ in the $C^{\infty}$ topology. Does $\overline{G}$ have empty interior in $\mathrm{Diff}^{\infty}_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$? Equivalently, is the set of $C^{\infty}$ diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}^n$ isotopic to the identity that possess at least one periodic point dense in $\mathrm{Diff}^{\infty}_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a form of the $C^{\infty}$ closing problem on the torus. For the area-preserving (and Hamiltonian) case on $\mathbb{T}^2$, a $C^{\infty}$ closing lemma has been established (Asaoka–Irie and subsequent work), showing density of diffeomorphisms with periodic points among area-preserving diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity. However, the general (non-conservative) $C^{\infty}$ closing problem on $\mathbb{T}^n$ for $n \geq 2$ in $\mathrm{Diff}^{\infty}_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ appears to remain open; sources note that whether the $C^r$-interior of aperiodic diffeomorphisms is empty is unknown for $r \geq 2$ on $\mathbb{T}^2$.

status_evidence.title: A C^∞ closing lemma on torus
status_evidence.snippet: A C^∞ closing lemma is proved for area-preserving diffeomorphisms on T^2 isotopic to the identity; periodic orbits are dense for a generic such diffeomorphism.
status_evidence.claim: The C^∞ closing problem is settled in the area-preserving case on T^2.

status_evidence.title: A C^∞ closing lemma for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of closed surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Asaoka–Irie establish a C^∞ closing lemma for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of closed surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: C^∞ closing lemma known in the Hamiltonian/area-preserving setting.

status_evidence.title: Pugh closing lemma - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: The C^r closing problem for r ≥ 2 is widely open; only the C^1 case is fully resolved by Pugh.
status_evidence.claim: General C^∞ closing problem remains open in higher regularity.
